activity_b.text: Good morning, please have a seat.
I’m Mr. Senarath, the electrical training supervisor.
How are you feeling today?
Good morning, sir. I’m doing fine, thank you.
I’m a little nervous, but I’m ready to try my best.
That’s perfectly alright.
This is a friendly interview.
So, Ramesh, I see that you completed school last year.
Can you tell me a bit about your background?
Yes, sir. I completed my A/Ls in August.
During my final year, I worked part-time with a small electrical maintenance team in Kurunegala.
I don’t have much experience yet, but I can handle basic electrical tasks safely.
Good to hear.
What kind of work did you support during your time there?
I assisted the electrician with wiring new circuits, fixing loose switches, and replacing worn-out sockets.
I also helped pull cables through conduits and sometimes labelled wires in the distribution board.
When the workload increased, I checked toolkits and prepared insulation tape and testers for the team.
I wasn’t in charge of major repairs, but I always supported the team whenever they needed help.
Excellent.
What skills do you think you can bring to our training programme?
I can test voltage levels using a multimeter, sir.
I know how to identify faulty connections, and I recently started learning how to install miniature circuit breakers.
I also learnt how to stay calm when dealing with tight deadlines.
I might need some guidance with reading full wiring diagrams and troubleshooting complex faults, but I’m going to improve quickly.
That’s a positive attitude.
How comfortable are you with earthing systems and basic panel work?
I’m not fully confident yet, but I can already handle simple panel tasks and basic earthing checks.
I might take more time with advanced control panels and three-phase systems.
That’s understandable.
What are your plans for the next few years?
I’m going to complete this training programme and then apply for an apprenticeship.
I might also follow short electrical safety courses to strengthen my technical skills.
That sounds good.
Thank you, Ramesh. We’ll contact you soon.
Thank you very much, sir. I appreciate the opportunity.
